channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Celina sobre Caio Bonfim no Mundial de Marcha Atlética: "Ele é ouro". Veja vídeo
item.description: Governor Celina Leão praised Olympic medalist Caio Bonfim after his bronze medal win at the 2026 World Race Walking Team Championships, calling his effort 'gold' in the hearts of the people. She emphasized the event's historic significance for Brasília, reinforcing the city's status as a sports hub and highlighting the role of family, faith, and public support in the athlete's journey.

item.title: O encontro de Flávio Bolsonaro com empresários em São Paulo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for the presidency, met with business leaders at the residence of Paulo Skaf, president of Fiesp, in São Paulo. The meeting included numerous national industry leaders, where the pre-candidate shared his vision for Brazil's future. According to Skaf, Flávio made a positive impression on attendees, many of whom had not met him before.

item.title: Pós-rachadinha: subsecretário, Queiroz monitora Guarda Municipal no RJ
item.description: Four years after being cleared in the 'rachadinha' investigation at Alerj, retired military police officer Fabricio Queiroz serves as subsecretary of Security and Public Order in Saquarema, RJ, overseeing the Municipal Guard and attending events with Bolsonarist leaders. His appointment was negotiated by former mayor Antonio Peres and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, highlighting the PL’s dominance in the city. Despite being the first alternate in his 2024 city council run, Queiroz was installed in the executive role, maintaining close ties with figures like Cláudio Castro and Marcelo Menezes.

item.title: Datafolha: 59% defendem prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro; 37% são contra
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows 59% of Brazilians support house arrest for Jair Bolsonaro, while 37% oppose it. Among centrist voters, 53% favor home detention and 41% oppose it. Bolsonaro supporters overwhelmingly (94%) back the measure, while 68% of Lula’s voters believe he should return to prison.

item.title: Flávio critica Lula com vídeo sobre fome gravado no governo Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro criticized the Lula government using a 2021 video showing people scavenging food from trash, blaming Lula for current misery despite the footage being filmed during his father Jair Bolsonaro’s presidency. Minister Guilherme Boulos demanded a retraction, accusing Flávio of misleadingly using old footage. The senator also linked Lula to rising household debt, citing a CNC survey showing 80.2% of Brazilian families were indebted in February 2026.

item.title: Gilmar sai em defesa de Jorge Messias e rebate ‘críticas vazias’ da imprensa
item.description: Minister Gilmar Mendes defended Attorney General Jorge Messias, nominated for the STF, calling press criticism 'empty and hasty'. He praised Messias’s technical record, respect for the separation of powers, and work on national sovereignty and holding big tech accountable. The Senate hearing is scheduled for April 29, with strong expectations of approval.

item.title: Datafolha: 59% defende prisão domiciliar para Bolsonaro enquanto 37% quer que ele volte para presídio
item.description: A Datafolha poll released this Sunday showed that 59% of Brazilians believe former President Jair Bolsonaro should serve his sentence under house arrest, while 37% think he should return to prison. Another 5% did not know how to respond. The survey interviewed 2,004 people between April 7 and 9 and has a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes defende ‘credenciais’ de Jorge Messias para vaga no Supremo
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes publicly defended Jorge Messias's nomination to the STF, emphasizing his qualifications, public administration experience, academic background, and role as Attorney General, including defense of national sovereignty and action against big techs. Mendes stated Messias is fit for the position and that the Senate will assess his merits, amid government efforts to advance the confirmation hearing scheduled for April 29.

item.title: Como os brasileiros avaliam a prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: According to a Datafolha poll released on April 12, 2026, 59% of Brazilians believe former President Jair Bolsonaro should serve his 27-year and three-month sentence under house arrest for leading an attempted coup. Another 37% say he should return to prison, while 5% were undecided. The survey interviewed 2,004 people across 137 municipalities from April 7 to 9, with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes defende indicação de Messias ao STF: "À altura do cargo"
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes defended the nomination of Jorge Messias, current head of the AGU, to a vacancy on the Federal Supreme Court, highlighting his extensive public administration experience, solid academic background, and conciliatory profile. Mendes stated that Messias is 'up to the position' and possesses the conditions to exercise judicial duties with balance, responsibility, and high institutional sense, especially amid challenges such as U.S. tariffs and actions against big techs. The CCJ Senate hearing is scheduled for April 29.

item.title: Gilmar sai em defesa de Messias: “Está à altura do cargo”
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes defended the appointment of Attorney General Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Tribunal, criticizing media critiques as 'empty and hasty'. He praised Messias’ qualified resume, extensive public service experience, leadership at the AGU, efforts to hold big techs accountable for illegal content, and defense of national sovereignty, stating Messias is 'up to the position' with balance, responsibility, and strong institutional sense.

item.title: Lula melhorou nas redes sociais, diz prefeito tiktoker de Sorocaba
item.description: Sorocaba Mayor Rodrigo Manga (Republicanos) praised President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) improved social media performance over the past two years, citing his charisma and fitness-related videos, but stated he will vote for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 presidential election. Manga said Lula and Bolsonaro are tied in online communication and expects a tight race between them. He also mentioned his return to office after being removed over health-related corruption allegations, which were overturned by the Supreme Court.

item.title: Gilmar defende Messias no STF e critica “leituras rasas” sobre indicação
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes defended the nomination of Jorge Messias as Attorney General of the Union, criticizing "shallow readings" of the appointment. Messias, nominated by President Lula, still awaits a Senate hearing on April 29 for approval to the STF vacancy.

item.title: Delegado conclui pela 2ª vez que não houve interferência de Bolsonaro na PF
item.description: The Federal Police concluded for the second time that there is no evidence of undue interference by former President Jair Bolsonaro in the institution, even after the case was reopened by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes. Delegate Carlos Henrique Pinheiro de Melo stated that the investigations carried out did not reveal elements sufficient to justify criminal charges, and that any potential acts should be investigated in related proceedings. The case has been forwarded to Attorney General Paulo Gonet for review and possible final dismissal.

item.title: ‘Falta coração na chuteira’, diz Marco Aurélio de Carvalho sobre ministros de Lula
item.description: Marco Aurélio de Carvalho, president of the Prerrogativas group, criticized the lack of engagement by Lula's government ministers in defending the administration's actions, stating that 'there's a lack of heart in the cleat' and urging them to take to the streets to better communicate the government's achievements. He acknowledged communication shortcomings but emphasized real advances in infrastructure, education, and international standing. While Lula leads in the first round per Datafolha, he trails Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff, though Carvalho remains optimistic about Lula's growth before the election.

item.title: O dia em que o Senado derrubou Alexandre de Moraes
item.description: The article reports that Alexandre de Moraes was initially rejected by the Senate in 2005 for the CNJ but later approved, and that over 20 years later, at least 50 pre-candidates for senator intend to use his potential removal from the STF as a campaign platform in the 2026 elections, leveraging the Court’s wear and tear and the Banco Master scandal to mobilize the far-right base.

item.title: O cálculo de aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre impeachment de ministros do STF e anistia
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro are crafting a strategy to ensure that, in the event of a 'Zero Um' (Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva) victory, the amnesty project for Bolsonarists is not annulled by the Supreme Federal Court (STF). The plan involves electing a senatorial bloc favorable to impeaching STF ministers—particularly Alexandre de Moraes—to alter the Court’s composition and enable Congress to pass the amnesty bill. The PL aims to elect 25 senators and secure at least 20 allies to reach the 54 votes needed to initiate impeachment proceedings against justices.

item.title: Senado aprova projeto que inclui criança como agravante de crime
item.description: The Senate approved a bill that includes the presence of a child or adolescent as an aggravating circumstance in crimes, even if they are not direct victims. Bill 4.244/2025, introduced by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, received a favorable report from Senator Magno Malta and is now headed to the Constitution and Justice Committee. The proposal also amends the Drug Law to increase penalties when minors are present during drug-related offenses.

item.title: Fachin barra tentativa de declarar Moraes suspeito em caso do 8 de Janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin rejected a request to declare Justice Alexandre de Moraes biased in a case related to the January 8, 2023 attacks. The request was made by defendant José Celso Cornolo Júnior, who claimed Moraes had political antagonism. Fachin ruled that social media mentions and news reports alone do not establish bias.

item.title: Datafolha: 40% avaliam governo Lula como ruim ou péssimo; 29% como ótimo ou bom
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on April 11 shows that 40% of voters evaluate Lula's government as bad or terrible, while 29% rate it as good or excellent. Negative assessment remained stable compared to March, but positive assessment dropped from 32% to 29%. Disapproval of Lula's performance reached 51%, versus 45% approval, with higher disapproval among the more educated, southerners, evangelicals, and those earning over 10 minimum wages.

item.title: Advogado nega envolvimento de filho de Lula em esquema do INSS
item.description: Lawyer Marco Aurélio de Carvalho denied any involvement of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, son of President Lula, in the INSS fraud scheme, stating that the Federal Police found no evidence to support the allegations. He emphasized that accusations against the president’s son are repetitive and unfounded, noting that Fábio Luiz has consistently cooperated with authorities and that the reported R$ 19 million in financial movements is inflated due to double-counting by Coaf, with actual movement being significantly lower. The lawyer affirmed the funds are legally sourced from inheritance, legitimate presidential advances, and asset sales from companies cleared in the Lava Jato case.

item.title: Governo precisa reduzir a percepção de que a vida não está boa
item.description: Former minister Gilberto Carvalho resigned from the National Secretariat of Popular and Solidarity Economy to join Lula’s re-election campaign coordination, focusing on dialogue with social movements. He emphasized that the government is preparing a debt renegotiation program, including up to 90% discounts on credit card, overdraft, and personal loan debts, using public resources as partial guarantees, to counter the perception that life is not improving amid rising household indebtedness, which reached 80.4% in March.

item.title: Datafolha vai medir pela primeira vez como brasileiro vê cada um dos 10 ministros do STF
item.description: The Datafolha Institute will conduct, for the first time, a survey to measure public evaluation of the ten ministers of the STF, including questions on performance, recognition, and suspicions of involvement in the Banco Master case. The focus is on Minister Alexandre de Moraes, whose image has been affected by contracts between his wife and banker Daniel Vorcaro and by the meteoric growth of his family's wealth. Recent polls show increasing concern over judicial power concentration as a threat to democracy, surpassing even corruption in public perception.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes defende Messias no STF: 'Senado saberá analisar seus múltiplos atributos'
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes defended the approval of Jorge Messias as a new minister of the Court, highlighting his work at the AGU in defending national sovereignty and combating big techs over criminal social media posts. Messias, nominated by Lula, must be approved by the Senate in a hearing scheduled for April 29, with a rapporteur designated in the CCJ.

item.title: O alerta de Simone Tebet sobre um ajuste fiscal ‘rigoroso’ em 2027
item.description: Simone Tebet warns that the next government will need to implement a more rigorous fiscal adjustment in 2027, particularly through reducing tax expenditures, which amount to around 520 billion reais annually. She defends that the Lula administration managed to significantly reduce the fiscal deficit thanks to the new fiscal framework, despite criticism over spending, and emphasizes that the window of opportunity for this adjustment will open after the 2026 elections.

item.title: Zema tem 4% no primeiro turno, aponta Datafolha
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) recorded 4% voting intention in the first round of the 2026 presidential election, according to Datafolha. This marks a slight decline from the previous survey, where he stood at 5%. President Lula leads the stimulated scenario.

item.title: Racha na direita expõe disputa por poder e eleva Nikolas Ferreira, dizem analistas
item.description: Brazil's right wing is experiencing an internal leadership struggle, with Deputy Nikolas Ferreira rising as a prominent figure and creating tension with Flávio Bolsonaro, whose presidential bid is threatened by the fragmentation of Bolsonarism. Analysts note that Ferreira's ascent, driven by digital popularity and mobilization capacity, challenges the movement's traditional loyalty-based structure and risks alienating centrist parties like União Brasil, PP, and Republicanos. Minas Gerais is highlighted as a key battleground state where right-wing unity is essential for electoral success.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cresce 38,1% em nº de seguidores em 6 meses
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro grew 38.1% in social media followers from October 2025 to March 2026, reaching 16.6 million, driven by his pre-candidacy announcement and Pablo Marçal’s endorsement. Despite having less than half of Lula’s 30.8 million followers, he achieved higher engagement, with nearly 50 million interactions in two months, surpassing Lula’s 28.2 million.

item.title: Delegado revisa inquérito e conclui pela segunda vez que não houve interferência de Bolsonaro na PF
item.description: The Federal Police, under the Lula administration, reviewed the investigation into alleged interference by Jair Bolsonaro in the agency and concluded, for the second time, that there is no evidence of criminal conduct. Delegado Carlos Henrique Pinheiro de Melo reiterated that prior investigations failed to uncover grounds for criminal liability, noting also the lack of evidence in the fake news inquiry referenced by the STF. The case has been forwarded to Attorney General Paulo Gonet for review and potential final dismissal.

item.title: PL ganha 44 mil filiados após pré-candidatura de Flávio ao Planalto
item.description: The PL gained 44,092 new members following Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-candidacy for president, reaching 939,614 total affiliates. Meanwhile, the PT lost 4,953 supporters but remains Brazil’s second-largest party with 1,668,670 members. By March 2026, Brazil had 16,063,752 party affiliates, with a net positive balance of 16,213 people, driven largely by the PL’s growth offsetting losses in other parties.

item.title: Zucco oficializa candidatura ao governo do RS em evento com Flávio
item.description: Federal deputy Luciano Zucco (PL-RS) officially launched his pre-candidacy for governor of Rio Grande do Sul in an event in Porto Alegre, alongside Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who is a pre-candidate for president. Zucco, elected federal deputy in 2022 with the highest vote count in the state, aims to solidify his campaign with Bolsonarist support in Rio Grande do Sul.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: após novo Datafolha, como fica a disputa Lula x Flávio
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro narrowly leading Lula in a simulated second-round runoff (46% to 45%), though the difference falls within the margin of error. Both candidates exhibit high and nearly identical rejection rates (Lula: 48%, Flávio: 46%), reflecting a polarized electorate with limited room for growth. Lula maintains a consistent lead in first-round projections across recent polls, despite gradual erosion in support over recent months.

item.title: Lula mantém avaliação negativa em 40%, mas aprovação recua para 29%, aponta Datafolha
item.description: President Lula's government approval dropped to 29%, with negative evaluation steady at 40%, according to a new Datafolha poll. His personal approval fell to 45% and disapproval rose to 51%, especially among the educated, Southerners, evangelicals and high-income earners. Nevertheless, Lula's ratings remain better than Bolsonaro's at the same stage of their presidencies.

item.title: Moraes barra visita de três deputados a Filipe Martins
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied visitation requests from three federal deputies to Filipe Martins, former aide to Jair Bolsonaro, held at Ponta Grossa Public Prison. While 14 lawmakers were granted access, the requests by Gustavo Gayer (PL), Marcel van Hattem (Novo), and an unnamed deputy were rejected. The ruling underscores judicial oversight over access to detainees in politically sensitive cases.

item.title: Datafolha: Avaliação negativa do governo Lula se mantém em 40%; positiva passa de 32% a 29%
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows that Lula's government negative rating remains at 40%, while positive approval dropped from 32% to 29%. Regular evaluation rose from 26% to 29%, and undecided respondents increased from 1% to 2%.

item.title: PT minimiza Datafolha que aponta avanço de Flávio sobre Lula
item.description: The national president of the PT, Edinho Silva, downplayed a Datafolha poll showing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) narrowly ahead of President Lula (PT) in a potential runoff scenario. The survey indicates a technical tie, with Bolsonaro at 46% and Lula at 44% in voter intention. Silva argued the poll does not reflect electoral reality and expressed confidence in the PT's re-election prospects.

item.title: Como estava a popularidade de FHC, Dilma e Bolsonaro a esta altura de seus mandatos
item.description: The April 2024 Datafolha poll shows President Lula with 29% positive and 40% negative approval, with 29% rating his government as regular, less than six months before the 2026 election. Lula’s current popularity is lower than in his first two terms (37% and 76% positive), but similar to FHC’s first term (38%), slightly above Dilma’s (41%) and significantly above Bolsonaro’s (25%) at comparable points in their presidencies.

item.title: Alçados a governadores, nove ex-vices têm seis meses para deixar a sombra dos padrinhos
item.description: Nine former vice-governors who assumed office after titular resignations in 2022 have six months to establish themselves as re-election candidates in 2026, facing the challenge of stepping out of their political godfathers' shadows and gaining electoral autonomy. In Minas Gerais, Mateus Simões (PSD), despite endorsements from Romeu Zema (Novo), struggles to rise in polls, with voter intentions below 10%. In Pará, Barbalho’s successor also struggles to maintain the predecessor’s high approval ratings, despite a strong legacy of governability.

item.title: A popularidade de Lula a menos de 6 meses da eleição, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows Lula's government negative rating remains at 40%, while positive approval dropped from 32% to 29% since March. His personal approval also declined slightly from 47% to 45%, within the margin of error. Higher disapproval is seen among the more educated, southerners, evangelicals, and high-income earners.

item.title: Lula tem 40% de avaliação negativa, indica Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on April 11 shows that 40% of Brazilians negatively evaluate Lula's government, unchanged from the previous survey. Positive approval dropped from 32% to 29%, while the share rating the government as regular rose from 26% to 29%. The full breakdown of the poll was not disclosed in the provided excerpt.

item.title: Alcolumbre encerra CPI do Crime Organizado sem prorrogação
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre decided not to extend the Organized Crime CPI, which will conclude on April 14. Rapporteur Alessandro Vieira criticized the decision as a disservice to Brazil but ruled out judicial appeal, stating that extension is a political decision of the Senate president. Vieira also hopes the STF will authorize a CPI to investigate Banco Master.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a presidential candidate, stated in an interview on the 'Inteligência Ltda' podcast that President Jair Messias Bolsonaro will climb the ramp of the Planalto Palace alongside him in January 2025. The remark was made during the recording of the episode aired on Monday, April 6.

item.title: A sensação de Lula após conversa com Moraes sobre o caso Master
item.description: Lula spoke with Minister Alexandre de Moraes about the Master case, involving former minister Anderson Torres, and received advice not to let the case damage his historical biography built after the January 8th ruling. He left the meeting with the impression that Moraes plans to act against government adversaries. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Kotscho: E se Lula desistir da reeleição, quem entra no seu lugar?
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva admitted for the first time that he may not run for re-election in 2026, stating in an ICL interview that 'I still don't know if I will be a candidate'. The remark, made six months before the election, has sparked speculation about who might replace him on the Workers' Party ticket.

item.title: Nova ida de Flávio aos EUA preocupa direita por radicalismo de Eduardo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro plans to travel to the United States to ask his brother Eduardo for moderation, after right-wing allies expressed concern that the meeting could radicalize his rhetoric. Flávio was recently labeled an 'entreguista' for making pro-U.S. statements at a conservative event, whose text was written by Eduardo, drawing criticism from leftists and allies who fear he will lose his image of balance as a pre-candidate. Despite the concern, the trip is seen as necessary to counter Eduardo’s radicalism and prevent a split in the right.

item.title: Caiado e Flávio
item.description: A poll conducted with 265 readers of Blog do Noblat shows that 67.5% believe Ronaldo Caiado’s presidential candidacy does not threaten Flávio Bolsonaro’s, while 32.5% see it as a threat. The survey was published alongside an interview with Caiado at the Metro­poles studio, highlighting internal conservative debate over right-wing leadership ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Queda na abstenção impulsionou peso do Nordeste em eleições
item.description: Northeast Brazil's participation in presidential elections increased significantly from 2002 to 2022, driven by declining abstention and rising education levels, while the Southeast saw a drop in electoral participation. Preliminary 2026 data suggest the Southeast will continue losing electoral weight, with 41.9% of eligible voters compared to 43 million in the Northeast. The Northeast's participation rate advanced 2.5 percentage points in second-round votes, outperforming other regions despite modest growth in the North and Center-West.

item.title: Produtor da carne paca servida por Janja na Páscoa é um velho amigo de Lula; saiba quem é
item.description: A video of First Lady Janja preparing paca meat for Lula at the Granja do Torto sparked controversy on social media, especially among environmentalists who criticized the consumption of game meat. Janja later clarified that the paca came from an Ibama-authorized producer. The producer mentioned is a longtime friend of Lula.

item.title: Quase meio milhão de usuários já se bloquearam de bets em plataforma do governo
item.description: Nearly half a million users have already self-excluded from online betting platforms through the Brazilian government's system, reflecting growing concern over rising debt linked to gambling. President Lula stated that, if it were up to him, he would shut down betting houses, but acknowledged the decision depends on Congress and is unlikely to happen. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Galípolo enfrenta forte pressão do entorno de Lula; saiba os motivos
item.description: Gabriel Galípolo, president of Brazil's Central Bank, is facing strong pressure from President Lula's inner circle, mainly for failing to cut interest rates — an opportunity now seen as lost, worsened by the Middle East conflict. A member of Lula's staff reportedly said Galípolo 'doesn't help the campaign at all'. The exclusive article highlights growing political discomfort with the BC's stance.
